Government Clarifies Passport Not Proof of Citizenship, Sparks Debate

The Indian government has clarified that a passport is primarily a travel document and not conclusive proof of Indian citizenship, citing the 1967 Passports Act and a Bombay High Court decision. This statement, made by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), has intensified a debate over what documents establish citizenship. While government sources stressed this point, some NRIs and opposition leaders have questioned what then serves as definitive proof of citizenship, leading to discussions about other documents like Aadhaar, PAN, and voter cards.
